newsitem.title: FRANCE: MINALI WINS STAGE AS ANOTHER ACCIDENT HITS TOUR DE FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: MINALI WINS STAGE AS ANOTHER ACCIDENT HITS TOUR DE FRANCE.

text.p: Italian sprint specialist Nicola Minali posted a photo-finish victory in the fourth stage of the Tour de France as another crash, this time involving a spectator, marred the cycling classic Wednesday.

Minali, who won a stage in Portsmouth, England in the 1994 Tour, nipped Frenchman Frederic Moncassin with Germany's Erik Zabel third after the 140-mile leg from Plumelec which was covered in five hours, 46 minutes and 42 seconds.
Mario Cipollini of Italy finished fourth but retained the overall lead over Zabel.
Zabel's result, worth a deduction of eight seconds, cut Cipollini's overall lead from 14 seconds to four seconds.

Banesto's Spanish rider Vicente Garcia-Acosta, in his first Tour, followed Swiss veteran Tony Rominger, victim of a mass pile-up Tuesday, out of the race after a crash and was taken to hospital in Nantes.

Garcia-Acosta and Italian Fabiano Fontanelli, who was later able to continue the race, both crashed into a woman spectator on the edge of the road around the 55-mile mark. The woman, who suffered a serious head injury, was also taken to hospital.

Cipollini, who has worn the yellow jersey since winning the first stage Sunday, and Zabel battled throughout the stage for the time deductions at the three intermediate sprints with the German taking two seconds more than the Italian.

A disappointed Moncassin, who has finished fourth, third and second in the stages, said: "I was strong in the sprint but it was Minali who took it in the end. Yesterday it was Zabel and before that Cipollini. I'm really disappointed."

The stage started at an easy pace, averaging 20 mph. After the crash, Rominger's Cofidis teammate Philippe Gaumont made a solo break that 60 miles from the finish had him a remarkable 11 minutes, 20 seconds ahead, virtually the time by which he trailed Cipollini.
But the peloton recovered the pace of the previous stages and with 30 miles to go, Gaumont held a mere 3.5-minute lead before being reined in and disappearing into the anonimity of the huge peloton.
With Cipollini holding a slim lead, Thursday's fifth stage over 162 miles to Chatre should feature a sprinters' battle for his yellow jersey.
